sanskrit: arthamūlo 'pahiṃsāṃ ca kurute svayam ātmanaḥ karair aśāstradṛṣṭair hi mohāt saṃpīḍayan prajāḥ
english: Driven by greed for wealth, he works his own undoing, for in his folly he oppresses the people with levies that the scriptures nowhere sanction.

sanskrit: ūdhaś chindyād dhi yo dhenvāḥ kṣīrārthī na labhet payaḥ evaṃ rāṣṭram ayogena pīḍitaṃ na vivardhate
english: For he who, craving milk, should cut away the cow's udder would get no milk at all; just so a realm afflicted by misrule does not thrive.

sanskrit: yo hi dogdhrīm upāste tu sa nityaṃ labhate payaḥ evaṃ rāṣṭram upāyena bhuñjāno labhate phalam
english: But he who tends the milch cow with care wins milk continually; even so, the king who draws upon his realm with prudent means reaps its fruit.

sanskrit: atha rāṣṭram upāyena bhujyamānaṃ surakṣitam janayaty atulāṃ nityaṃ kośavṛddhiṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: A realm well guarded and enjoyed by skilful means, Yudhiṣṭhira, ever brings forth an unmatched increase of the treasury.

sanskrit: dogdhi dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca prajā rājñi surakṣitā nityaṃ svebhyaḥ parebhyaś ca tṛptā mātā yathā payaḥ
english: The people, well protected by the king, yield him grain and gold, as a contented mother yields her milk freely to her own and to others alike.

sanskrit: mālākāropamo rājan bhava māṅgārikopamaḥ tathā yuktaś ciraṃ rāṣṭraṃ bhoktuṃ śakyasi pālayan
english: Be like the gardener, O king, not like the charcoal-burner; so disposed, you will be able, by protecting your realm, to enjoy it long.

sanskrit: paracakrābhiyānena yadi te syād dhanakṣayaḥ atha sāmnaiva lipsethā dhanam abrāhmaṇeṣu yat
english: If, through a campaign against a hostile power, your wealth should be exhausted, then by conciliation alone should you seek to gather what wealth lies among men who are not brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: mā sma te brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanasthaṃ pracalen manaḥ antyāyām apy avasthāyāṃ kim u sphītasya bhārata
english: Let not your mind waver at the sight of a brāhmaṇa possessed of wealth, not even in the direst extremity, O Bhārata, and how much less when you are prosperous?

sanskrit: dhanāni tebhyo dadyās tvaṃ yathāśakti yathārhataḥ sāntvayan parirakṣaṃś ca svargam āpsyasi durjayam
english: Rather should you give wealth to them according to your power and their desert; consoling and protecting them, you will attain heaven, hard though it be to win.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmeṇa vṛttena prajās tvaṃ paripālayan svantaṃ puṇyaṃ yaśovantaṃ prāpsyase kurunandana
english: Thus, by conduct grounded in dharma, protecting the people, you will attain an end that is good, meritorious, and crowned with renown, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa prajāḥ pālaya pāṇḍava yudhiṣṭhira tathā yukto nādhibandhena yokṣyase
english: Protect the people through righteous administration, O Pāṇḍava; so engaged, Yudhiṣṭhira, you will not be bound by the fetters of sorrow.

sanskrit: eṣa eva paro dharmo yad rājā rakṣate prajāḥ bhūtānāṃ hi yathā dharme rakṣaṇaṃ ca parā dayā
english: This indeed is the supreme dharma, that the king protect his people; for the protection of beings in accordance with dharma is the highest compassion.

sanskrit: tasmād evaṃ paraṃ dharmaṃ manyante dharmakovidāḥ yad rājā rakṣaṇe yukto bhūteṣu kurute dayām
english: Therefore those skilled in dharma hold this to be the supreme dharma: that the king, devoted to protection, shows compassion toward all beings.

sanskrit: yad ahnā kurute pāpam arakṣan bhayataḥ prajāḥ rājā varṣasahasreṇa tasyāntam adhigacchati
english: The sin a king commits in a single day by failing to guard the people from fear—only after a thousand years does he reach the end of its consequence.

sanskrit: yad ahnā kurute puṇyaṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tasya bhuṅkte phalaṃ divi
english: The merit a king earns in a single day by protecting the people righteously—its fruit he enjoys in heaven for ten thousand years.

sanskrit: sviṣṭiḥ svadhītiḥ sutapā lokāñ jayati yāvataḥ kṣaṇena tān avāpnoti prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: Whatever worlds are won by him who has sacrificed well, studied well, and practised austerity—those a king attains in a moment by protecting the people righteously.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmaṃ prayatnena kaunteya paripālayan iha puṇyaphalaṃ labdhvā nādhibandhena yokṣyase
english: Thus diligently upholding dharma, O son of Kuntī, having gained the fruit of merit here, you will not be bound by the fetters of sorrow.

sanskrit: svargaloke ca mahatīṃ śriyaṃ prāpsyasi pāṇḍava asaṃbhavaś ca dharmāṇām īdṛśānām arājasu tasmād rājaiva nānyo 'sti yo mahat phalam āpnuyāt
english: And in the world of heaven you will attain great splendour, O Pāṇḍava. Duties such as these are impossible for those who are not kings; therefore it is the king alone, and no other, who can win so vast a reward.

sanskrit: sa rājyam ṛddhimat prāpya dharmeṇa paripālayan indraṃ tarpaya somena kāmaiś ca suhṛdo janān
english: Having won a flourishing kingdom and ruling it righteously, gratify Indra with the soma offering, and your friends and people with the fulfilment of their desires.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ya eva tu sato rakṣed asataś ca nibarhayet sa eva rājñā kartavyo rājan rājapurohitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: He who would protect the good and root out the wicked—he alone, O king, is the man the king should appoint as his royal chaplain.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam purūravasa ailasya saṃvādaṃ mātariśvanaḥ
english: On this point too they recite an ancient tale: the dialogue between Purūravas, son of Ilā, and Mātariśvan, the Wind.

sanskrit: aila uvāca kutaḥ svid brāhmaṇo jāto varṇāś cāpi kutas trayaḥ kasmāc ca bhavati śreyān etad vāyo vicakṣva me
english: The son of Ilā said: Whence was the brāhmaṇa born, and whence the other three classes? And by what cause is one superior to the rest? Explain this to me, O Wind.

sanskrit: vāyur uvāca brahmaṇo mukhataḥ sṛṣṭo brāhmaṇo rājasattama bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ sṛṣṭa ūrubhyāṃ vaiśya ucyate
english: The Wind said: From the mouth of Brahmā was the brāhmaṇa created, O best of kings; from his arms the kṣatriya was brought forth, and from his thighs, they say, the vaiśya.

sanskrit: varṇānāṃ paricaryārthaṃ trayāṇāṃ puruṣarṣabha varṇaś caturthaḥ paścāt tu padbhyāṃ śūdro vinirmitaḥ
english: To serve these three classes, O bull among men, the fourth class was fashioned thereafter: the śūdra, made from his feet.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo jātamātras tu pṛthivīm anvajāyata īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmakośasya guptaye
english: The brāhmaṇa, the very moment he was born, came into being upon the earth as lord over all creatures, for the safekeeping of the treasury of dharma.

sanskrit: tataḥ pṛthivyā goptāraṃ kṣatriyaṃ daṇḍadhāriṇam dvitīyaṃ varṇam akarot prajānām anuguptaye
english: Then he made the kṣatriya, the second class, as the protector of the earth and the wielder of the rod, for the guarding of the people.

sanskrit: vaiśyas tu dhanadhānyena trīn varṇān bibhṛyād imān śūdro hy enān paricared iti brahmānuśāsanam
english: The vaiśya should sustain these three classes with wealth and grain, and the śūdra should serve them—such is the ordinance of Brahmā.

sanskrit: aila uvāca dvijasya kṣatrabandhor vā kasyeyaṃ pṛthivī bhavet dharmataḥ saha vittena samyag vāyo pracakṣva me
english: The son of Ilā said: To whom does this earth, together with its wealth, rightfully belong—to the twice-born or to the kṣatriya? Tell me this truly, O Wind.

sanskrit: vāyur uvāca viprasya sarvam evaitad yat kiṃ cij jagatīgatam jyeṣṭhenābhijaneneha tad dharmakuśalā viduḥ
english: The Wind said: All this, whatever exists upon the earth, belongs to the brāhmaṇa; by reason of his birth as the eldest, those skilled in dharma know it to be his.

sanskrit: svam eva brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte svaṃ vaste svaṃ dadāti ca gurur hi sarvavarṇānāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaś ca vai dvijaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa enjoys only what is his own, wears what is his own, and gives away what is his own; for the twice-born is the guru of all the classes, eldest and most excellent.

sanskrit: patyabhāve yathā strī hi devaraṃ kurute patim ānantaryāt tathā kṣatraṃ pṛthivī kurute patim
english: As a woman, in the absence of her husband, takes the husband's brother as her lord, so the earth, by reason of succession, takes the kṣatriya as her lord.

sanskrit: eṣa te prathamaḥ kalpa āpady anyo bhaved ataḥ yadi svarge paraṃ sthānaṃ dharmataḥ parimārgasi
english: This is the first rule for you; another is meant for times of distress—if, by way of dharma, you seek the highest place in heaven.

sanskrit: yaḥ kaś cid vijayed bhūmiṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet śrutavṛttopapannāya dharmajñāya tapasvine
english: Whoever should conquer territory should make it over to a brāhmaṇa—one endowed with sacred learning and good conduct, knowing dharma and given to austerity—

sanskrit: svadharmaparitṛptāya yo na vittaparo bhavet yo rājānaṃ nayed buddhyā sarvataḥ paripūrṇayā
english: to one content in his own duty, who is not greedy for wealth, who could guide the king by an understanding complete in every respect.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hi kule jātaḥ kṛtaprajño vinītavāk śreyo nayati rājānaṃ bruvaṃś citrāṃ sarasvatīm
english: For a brāhmaṇa born in a good family, of ripened wisdom and disciplined speech, leads the king toward what is good, his eloquence flowing in wondrous strains.

sanskrit: rājā carati yaṃ dharmaṃ brāhmaṇena nidarśitam śuśrūṣur anahaṃvādī kṣatradharmavrate sthitaḥ
english: Whatever dharma the king practises as shown to him by the brāhmaṇa—being attentive, free of arrogant speech, and steadfast in the vow of kṣatriya duty—

sanskrit: tāvatā sa kṛtaprajñaś ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati tasya dharmasya sarvasya bhāgī rājapurohitaḥ
english: by that very measure he, grown wise, abides long in renown; and of all that dharma the royal chaplain is a sharer.

sanskrit: evam eva prajāḥ sarvā rājānam abhisaṃśritāḥ samyagvṛttāḥ svadharmasthā na kutaś cid bhayānvitāḥ
english: In just this way, all the people who take refuge in the king, conducting themselves well and abiding in their own duties, are beset by no fear from any quarter.

sanskrit: rāṣṭre caranti yaṃ dharmaṃ rājñā sādhv abhirakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya dharmasya rājā bhāgaṃ sa vindati
english: Whatever dharma they practise within the realm, well protected by the king—of that dharma the king obtains a fourth share.

sanskrit: devā manuṣyāḥ pitaro gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ yajñam evopajīvanti nāsti ceṣṭam arājake
english: Gods, men, ancestors, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas all live upon sacrifice—and there is no sacrifice where there is no king.

sanskrit: ito dattena jīvanti devatāḥ pitaras tathā rājany evāsya dharmasya yogakṣemaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: By what is offered from here the gods and likewise the ancestors live; and upon the king alone rests the securing and preserving of this dharma.

sanskrit: chāyāyām apsu vāyau ca sukham uṣṇe 'dhigacchati agnau vāsasi sūrye ca sukhaṃ śīte 'dhigacchati
english: In the heat one finds comfort in shade, in water, and in the breeze; in the cold one finds comfort in fire, in clothing, and in the sun.

sanskrit: śabde sparśe rase rūpe gandhe ca ramate manaḥ teṣu bhogeṣu sarveṣu nabhīto labhate sukham
english: The mind delights in sound, touch, taste, form, and smell; yet in all these enjoyments it is the man free of fear who finds true happiness.

sanskrit: abhayasyaiva yo dātā tasyaiva sumahat phalam na hi prāṇasamaṃ dānaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
english: He who is the giver of freedom from fear, his is the very greatest reward; for in the three worlds there is no gift equal to the gift of life.

sanskrit: indro rājā yamo rājā dharmo rājā tathaiva ca rājā bibharti rūpāṇi rājñā sarvam idaṃ dhṛtam
english: The king is Indra, the king is Yama, the king is Dharma himself; the king bears all these forms, and by the king is all this upheld.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rājñā purohitaḥ kāryo bhaved vidvān bahuśrutaḥ ubhau samīkṣya dharmārthāv aprameyāv anantaram
english: Bhīṣma said: The king should appoint as his chaplain one who is learned and deeply versed in scripture, who has weighed well both dharma and artha—both immeasurable—each in close relation to the other.

sanskrit: dharmātmā dharmavid yeṣāṃ rājñāṃ rājan purohitaḥ rājā caivaṃ guṇo yeṣāṃ kuśalaṃ teṣu sarvaśaḥ
english: Those kings whose chaplain is righteous of soul and knowing of dharma, and who are themselves endowed with such virtues—with them, O king, all is well in every way.

sanskrit: ubhau prajā vardhayato devān pūrvān parān pitṝn yau sameyāsthitau dharme śraddheyau sutapasvinau
english: Both together cause the people, the gods, and the ancestors near and far to flourish—the two who, joined together and steadfast in dharma, are worthy of trust and rich in austerity.

sanskrit: parasparasya suhṛdau saṃmatau samacetasau brahmakṣatrasya saṃmānāt prajāḥ sukham avāpnuyuḥ
english: Friends to each other, in mutual accord and of one mind—through the honour paid to brahman and kṣatra the people would attain happiness.

sanskrit: vimānanāt tayor eva prajā naśyeyur eva ha brahmakṣatraṃ hi sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ mūlam ucyate
english: But by the dishonouring of these two the people would surely perish; for brahman and kṣatra together are called the root of all duties.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ailakaśyapasaṃvādaṃ taṃ nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this point too they recite an ancient tale: the dialogue between the son of Ilā and Kaśyapa—mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: aila uvāca yadā hi brahma prajahāti kṣatraṃ; kṣatraṃ yadā vā prajahāti brahma anvag balaṃ katame 'smin bhajante; tathābalyaṃ katame 'smin viyanti
english: The son of Ilā said: When brahman forsakes kṣatra, or when kṣatra in turn forsakes brahman, which of the two then enjoys the stronger power, and through which of them does the weakness set in?

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca vyṛddhaṃ rāṣṭraṃ bhavati kṣatriyasya; brahma kṣatraṃ yatra virudhyate ha anvag balaṃ dasyavas tad bhajante; 'balyaṃ tathā tatra viyanti santaḥ
english: Kaśyapa said: Ruined becomes the realm of the kṣatriya wherein brahman and kṣatra fall into discord; there the brigands come to enjoy the power, and there the good men waste away into weakness.

sanskrit: naiṣām ukṣā vardhate nota usrā; na gargaro mathyate no yajante naiṣāṃ putrā vedam adhīyate ca; yadā brahma kṣatriyāḥ saṃtyajanti
english: Their bulls do not thrive, nor their cows; no churning-stick stirs the curds, nor do they sacrifice; nor do their sons study the Veda—when the kṣatriyas abandon brahman.

sanskrit: naiṣām ukṣā vardhate jātu gehe; nādhīyate saprajā no yajante apadhvastā dasyubhūtā bhavanti; ye brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyān saṃtyajanti
english: No bull thrives in their household ever; they do not study with their offspring, nor do they sacrifice; degraded, they become as brigands—those brāhmaṇas who abandon the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: etau hi nityasaṃyuktāv itaretaradhāraṇe kṣatraṃ hi brahmaṇo yonir yoniḥ kṣatrasya ca dvijāḥ
english: For these two are ever bound together in upholding each other: kṣatra is the womb of brahman, and the twice-born are the womb of kṣatra.

sanskrit: ubhāv etau nityam abhiprapannau; saṃprāpatur mahatīṃ śrīpratiṣṭhām tayoḥ saṃdhir bhidyate cet purāṇas; tataḥ sarvaṃ bhavati hi saṃpramūḍham
english: When these two are ever devoted to each other, they attain a great and firmly seated splendour; but if their ancient union is broken, then all falls into utter confusion.

sanskrit: nātra plavaṃ labhate pāragāmī; mahāgādhe naur iva saṃpraṇunnā cāturvarṇyaṃ bhavati ca saṃpramūḍhaṃ; tataḥ prajāḥ kṣayasaṃsthā bhavanti
english: Then he who would cross over finds no raft, like a boat cast adrift upon fathomless depths; the four-fold order falls into confusion, and thereupon the people are set on the path to ruin.

sanskrit: brahmavṛkṣo rakṣyamāṇo madhu hema ca varṣati arakṣyamāṇaḥ satatam aśru pāpaṃ ca varṣati
english: The tree of brahman, when guarded, rains down honey and gold; but left unguarded, it rains down only tears and evil without end.

sanskrit: abrahmacārī caraṇād apeto; yadā brahmā brahmaṇi trāṇam icchet āścaryaśo varṣati tatra devas; tatrābhīkṣṇaṃ duḥsahāś cāviśanti
english: When one who is no celibate, fallen away from right discipline, yet a brāhmaṇa, seeks protection within the brahman order, there the god rains only by rare chance, and there calamities hard to bear assail again and again.

sanskrit: striyaṃ hatvā brāhmaṇaṃ vāpi pāpaḥ; sabhāyāṃ yatra labhate 'nuvādam rājñaḥ sakāśe na bibheti cāpi; tato bhayaṃ jāyate kṣatriyasya
english: Where a sinner who has slain a woman or a brāhmaṇa finds approval in the assembly, and feels no fear even in the king's presence—from that does danger arise for the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: pāpaiḥ pāpe kriyamāṇe 'tivelaṃ; tato rudro jāyate deva eṣaḥ pāpaiḥ pāpāḥ saṃjanayanti rudraṃ; tataḥ sarvān sādhvasādhūn hinasti
english: When sin is wrought by sinners beyond all measure, then is this god Rudra born; the wicked by their wickedness bring forth Rudra, and then he destroys all alike, the good and the wicked.

sanskrit: aila uvāca kuto rudraḥ kīdṛśo vāpi rudraḥ; sattvaiḥ sattvaṃ dṛśyate vadhyamānam etad vidvan kaśyapa me pracakṣva; yato rudro jāyate deva eṣaḥ
english: The son of Ilā said: Whence is Rudra, and of what nature is this Rudra? By living beings the living are seen to be destroyed. Explain this to me, learned Kaśyapa—whence is this god Rudra born?

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca ātmā rudro hṛdaye mānavānāṃ; svaṃ svaṃ dehaṃ paradehaṃ ca hanti vātotpātaiḥ sadṛśaṃ rudram āhur; dāvair jīmūtaiḥ sadṛśaṃ rūpam asya
english: Kaśyapa said: Rudra is the self within the hearts of men; he slays both one's own body and the body of another. They call Rudra like the onslaughts of the wind; his form is like forest fires and like thunderclouds.

sanskrit: aila uvāca na vai vātaṃ parivṛnoti kaś cin; na jīmūto varṣati naiva dāvaḥ tathāyukto dṛśyate mānaveṣu; kāmadveṣād badhyate mucyate ca
english: The son of Ilā said: No one can wrap up the wind, nor does the thundercloud rain, nor the forest fire blaze, in the same fashion as is seen among men; for it is through desire and hatred that a man is bound and is set free.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca yathaikagehe jātavedāḥ pradīptaḥ; kṛtsnaṃ grāmaṃ pradahet sa tvarāvān vimohanaṃ kurute deva eṣa; tataḥ sarvaṃ spṛśyate puṇyapāpaiḥ
english: Kaśyapa said: As a fire blazing in a single house may swiftly burn down the whole village, so this god works delusion, and thereupon all are touched by merit and demerit together.

sanskrit: aila uvāca yadi daṇḍaḥ spṛśate puṇyabhājaṃ; pāpaiḥ pāpe kriyamāṇe 'viśeṣāt kasya hetoḥ sukṛtaṃ nāma kuryād; duṣkṛtaṃ vā kasya hetor na kuryāt
english: The son of Ilā said: If the rod of punishment touches the man of merit without distinction, when sin is wrought by sinners, then for what reason should one do good, and for what reason should one refrain from evil?

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca asaṃtyāgāt pāpakṛtām apāpāṃs; tulyo daṇḍaḥ spṛśate miśrabhāvāt śuṣkeṇārdraṃ dahyate miśrabhāvān; na miśraḥ syāt pāpakṛdbhiḥ kathaṃ cit
english: Kaśyapa said: Because the evildoers are not cast off, the same punishment touches the innocent through their commingling; the green is burned together with the dry by reason of their mingling. Let one therefore never mingle in any way with those who do evil.

sanskrit: aila uvāca sādhvasādhūn dhārayatīha bhūmiḥ; sādhvasādhūṃs tāpayatīha sūryaḥ sādhvasādhūn vātayatīha vāyur; āpas tathā sādhvasādhūn vahanti
english: The son of Ilā said: Here the earth bears up the good and the wicked alike; here the sun warms the good and the wicked alike; here the wind blows upon the good and the wicked alike, and the waters likewise carry the good and the wicked alike.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca evam asmin vartate loka eva; nāmutraivaṃ vartate rājaputra pretyaitayor antaravān viśeṣo; yo vai puṇyaṃ carate yaś ca pāpam
english: Kaśyapa said: Thus indeed it is in this world, but not so in the world beyond, O prince; after death there is a wide difference between the two—him who does good and him who does evil.

sanskrit: puṇyasya loko madhumān ghṛtārcir; hiraṇyajyotir amṛtasya nābhiḥ tatra pretya modate brahmacārī; na tatra mṛtyur na jarā nota duḥkham
english: The world of merit flows with honey, its flame is clarified butter, its light is gold, and it is the very navel of immortality; there, after death, the man of holy conduct rejoices—there is no death, no old age, and no sorrow.

sanskrit: pāpasya loko nirayo 'prakāśo; nityaṃ duḥkhaḥ śokabhūyiṣṭha eva tatrātmānaṃ śocate pāpakarmā; bahvīḥ samāḥ prapatann apratiṣṭhaḥ
english: The world of evil is hell, devoid of light, ever full of pain and abounding in grief; there the evildoer laments over himself, falling through many years without any foothold.

sanskrit: mitho bhedād brāhmaṇakṣatriyāṇāṃ; prajā duḥkhaṃ duḥsahaṃ cāviśanti evaṃ jñātvā kārya eveha vidvān; purohito naikavidyo nṛpeṇa
english: Through mutual discord between brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas the people enter into pain hard to bear; knowing this, the king should indeed here appoint as chaplain a learned man, not one of meagre knowledge.

sanskrit: taṃ caivānvabhiṣicyeta tathā dharmo vidhīyate agryo hi brāhmaṇaḥ proktaḥ sarvasyaiveha dharmataḥ
english: And he should consecrate such a one along with himself; so is the dharma ordained, for the brāhmaṇa is declared foremost of all here, by the law of dharma.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hi brāhmaṇāḥ sṛṣṭā iti dharmavido viduḥ jyeṣṭhenābhijanenāsya prāptaṃ sarvaṃ yad uttaram
english: For first of all were the brāhmaṇas created, so those who know dharma understand; and by reason of his birth as the eldest, all that is highest has come to him.

sanskrit: tasmān mānyaś ca pūjyaś ca brāhmaṇaḥ prasṛtāgrabhuk sarvaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaṃ ca nivedyaṃ tasya dharmataḥ
english: Therefore the brāhmaṇa is to be honoured and worshipped, the first to partake of the offered food; whatever is best and most excellent should, by dharma, be presented to him.

sanskrit: avaśyam etat kartavyaṃ rājñā balavatāpi hi brahma vardhayati kṣatraṃ kṣatrato brahma vardhate
english: This must without fail be done by the king, however mighty he may be; for brahman makes kṣatra to flourish, and from kṣatra brahman flourishes in turn.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yogakṣemo hi rāṣṭrasya rājanyāyatta ucyate yogakṣemaś ca rājño 'pi samāyattaḥ purohite
english: Bhīṣma said: The securing and preserving of the realm is said to rest upon the king; and the securing and preserving of the king himself rests upon the chaplain.

sanskrit: yatādṛṣṭaṃ bhayaṃ brahma prajānāṃ śamayaty uta dṛṣṭaṃ ca rājā bāhubhyāṃ tad rāṣṭraṃ sukham edhate
english: Where brahman quells the unseen dangers of the people, and the king with his two arms quells the seen, that realm thrives in happiness.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam mucukundasya saṃvādaṃ rājño vaiśravaṇasya ca
english: On this point too they recite an ancient tale: the dialogue between King Mucukunda and Vaiśravaṇa.
